simple.meaning: טָפַף (ṭâphaph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to trip (with short steps) coquettishly.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 3:16. The surrounding contexts include family line.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טָפַף (H2952) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: טָפַף (ṭâphaph) / H2952 is traced through Isaiah 3:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H2952. taphaph [ טָפַף ] verb trip, take quick little steps (compare Arabic pass by quickly , light, brisk, quick , of horse; possibly compare Syriac flicker ) — Qal Infinitive absolute טָפֹף Isa 3:16 תֵּלַכְנָה וְטָפֹף הָלוֺךְ , of women of Jerusalem.
